threads.body: this changelog seems to be wrong, it should mention specific attributes but mentions something unknown

Google's `Usage` also provides `cached_tokens_by_modality`, but this implementation maps only input/output breakdowns. Consequently the new text/image/audio cache-read attributes remain absent even when Google supplies them, despite the PR's stated goal of recording available modality usage; map that list to the three `*_cache_read_input_tokens` fields as well.

OpenAI exposes this field as `cache_write_tokens`, so reading `cache_write_input_tokens` drops real cache-write usage. Also, `or cache_creation` replaces a valid zero with the legacy value; fall back only when the new field is `None`.

This issue also appears on line 588 of the same file.

         return UsageTokens()
 
     details = usage.input_tokens_details
+    cache_creation = (
+        details.cache_creation_input_tokens
+        if details is not None
+        and hasattr(details, "cache_creation_input_tokens")
+        else None
+    )
+    cache_write = (
+        getattr(details, "cache_write_input_tokens", None)
+        if details is not None
+        else None
+    ) or cache_creation

Update that published API documentation so consumers can discover the new fields and deprecation.

replies.body:
In semantic conventions, agent spans only specify aggregate `input_tokens` and `output_tokens` (modality breakdowns and cache tokens are currently only specified on inference spans).

I think we should not add them to agents - these are breakdown things that don't make sense if aggregated across models
Removed cache tokens from `AgentInvocation._get_usage_attributes()` so they are not emitted on agent spans per semconv PR #469.
